description: Multi-word patterns and constructions that mark text as machine-generated. Each entry lists the phrase, a real-style example, and the fix.

phrases.example: It's not about the tool. It's about the system.
phrases.fix: State Y alone, or name the actor: 'The system decides outcomes, not the tool.'

phrases.phrase: X is not Y. It is Z.
phrases.example: The gap is not labor arbitrage. It is a trillion-parameter model that wakes only 32 billion parameters per token.
phrases.fix: State Z alone: 'The gap is architecture. A trillion-parameter model wakes only 32 billion parameters per token.'

phrases.phrase: X, Y, and Z, and [the point]
phrases.example: The AI cost gap is architecture, subsidies, and strategy, and most buyers are reading the wrong number.
phrases.fix: The real point was smuggled into a trailing 'and' clause. Promote it: 'Most buyers are reading the wrong number. The gap is architecture, subsidies, and strategy.'

phrases.example: The routing decision is now a monthly operating cost, not a one-time choice.
phrases.fix: Cut the negation tail: 'Routing is now a monthly operating cost. Teams make the decision every invoice cycle.'

phrases.example: The gap is structural, not just financial.
phrases.fix: State the claim alone: 'The gap is structural. The price difference is a symptom.'

phrases.example: Not just growth, but sustainable growth.
phrases.fix: Write the positive: 'Growth that compounds requires a system.'

phrases.example: That is not hype. That is a procurement decision validated by real performance data.
phrases.fix: State the positive alone: 'The data tells a procurement story, not a hype story.' Or rewrite without the binary contrast entirely.

phrases.example: It's not about the tool. It's about the system.
phrases.fix: State the positive alone: 'The system decides outcomes.'

phrases.example: This is not a partnership. This is an acquisition.
phrases.fix: Name what it is directly: 'This is an acquisition dressed as a partnership.'

phrases.phrase: The future isn't coming. It's already here.
phrases.example: The future of work isn't coming. It's already here.
phrases.fix: Give a concrete signal of change instead of a fortune-cookie line.

phrases.example: In today's competitive landscape, companies must adapt or die.
phrases.fix: Start with the actual situation: 'Margins are compressing across the industry.'

phrases.example: In today's fast-paced world, attention is scarce.
phrases.fix: Cut it. Make the claim: 'Attention is scarce.'

phrases.example: It's worth noting that costs rose 12%.
phrases.fix: Just state it: 'Costs rose 12%.'

phrases.example: It's important to note that the team shipped on time.
phrases.fix: State the fact. If it's important, the fact carries itself.

phrases.example: It should be noted that the API rate limit changed.
phrases.fix: Active voice: 'The API rate limit changed.'

phrases.example: Here's the thing: most teams don't measure this.
phrases.fix: State the thing.

phrases.example: Let me be clear: this is not sustainable.
phrases.fix: Say it plainly. The preface signals the opposite of clarity.

phrases.example: The best part: it costs nothing.
phrases.fix: Colon reveal. Say: 'It costs nothing.'

phrases.example: The catch: it only works in production.
phrases.fix: Name the constraint directly.

phrases.example: The key takeaway is that retention drives revenue.
phrases.fix: Say the takeaway.

phrases.phrase: What nobody tells you about X
phrases.example: What nobody tells you about fundraising is the time cost.
phrases.fix: Just deliver the insight: 'Fundraising is a full-time job on top of the company.'

phrases.example: The part everyone misses is the onboarding flow.
phrases.fix: Say the part: 'Onboarding decides retention.'

phrases.example: The truth is, most dashboards go unread.
phrases.fix: Cut the setup. State the fact.

phrases.example: When it comes to pricing, clarity wins.
phrases.fix: Start at the subject: 'Pricing rewards clarity.'

phrases.example: In the world of SaaS, retention is king.
phrases.fix: Cut the frame: 'Retention is king in SaaS.' Or just 'Retention decides SaaS outcomes.'

phrases.phrase: Whether you like it or not
phrases.example: Whether you like it or not, AI is here to stay.
phrases.fix: Drop the challenge frame; state the fact or drop it.

phrases.phrase: At the end of the day
phrases.example: At the end of the day, execution matters.
phrases.fix: Cut it.

phrases.example: In conclusion, we recommend waiting.
phrases.fix: Give the recommendation. The marker is scaffolding.

phrases.example: It goes without saying that security comes first.
phrases.fix: If it goes without saying, don't say it.

phrases.example: Needless to say, the launch was delayed.
phrases.fix: Say it or don't. The phrase wastes words.

phrases.example: With that in mind, let's look at the numbers.
phrases.fix: Transition filler. Cut or move forward.

phrases.example: In other words, the system is broken.
phrases.fix: Often signals repetition; say it once, better.

phrases.example: Let's dive into the details.
phrases.fix: Start with the details.

phrases.example: Without further ado, here's the plan.
phrases.fix: Cut it.

phrases.example: In today's digital age, data is king.
phrases.fix: Cut. State the claim.

phrases.example: Data is the new oil.
phrases.fix: Cliché formula. Say what X actually does.

phrases.phrase: The only thing standing between X and Y
phrases.example: The only thing standing between you and success is consistency.
phrases.fix: Cut the dramatic frame.

phrases.phrase: X is more than just Y
phrases.example: This is more than just a tool.
phrases.fix: Say what it is, then why it matters.

phrases.phrase: Whether you're a X or a Y
phrases.example: Whether you're a founder or a marketer, this applies.
phrases.fix: Pick the reader; don't spray both sides of every dichotomy.

phrases.example: From startups to enterprises, teams use this.
phrases.fix: Coverage claim; name who you mean.

phrases.phrase: Not just X, but also Y
phrases.example: Not just faster, but also more accurate.
phrases.fix: Split into two sentences or state the stronger claim.

phrases.example: Experts agree that hybrid work is here to stay.
phrases.fix: Name the experts or drop the appeal.

phrases.example: Studies show that remote teams are more productive.
phrases.fix: Cite the study or drop the claim.

phrases.example: Research suggests that AI adoption is accelerating.
phrases.fix: Cite or cut.

phrases.example: It is widely believed that the market will recover.
phrases.fix: Who believes it? Say who.

phrases.example: Some may argue that this is too aggressive.
phrases.fix: Name the position and engage with it, or cut.

phrases.example: In a world where attention is scarce, clarity wins.
phrases.fix: Start with the fact: 'Attention is scarce. Clarity wins.'

phrases.example: The bottom line is we need to move faster.
phrases.fix: Say the bottom line.

phrases.example: At its core, this is a trust problem.
phrases.fix: Say it without the intro: 'This is a trust problem.'

phrases.example: By its very nature, automation removes judgment.
phrases.fix: Cut 'by its very nature'.

phrases.example: It is what it is.
phrases.fix: It's a cop-out. Say what you'll do about it.

phrases.example: Easier said than done, but essential.
phrases.fix: Cut the cliché; give the first step.

phrases.example: Through the lens of growth, this matters.
phrases.fix: Cut the lens metaphor.

phrases.phrase: In the grand scheme of things
phrases.example: In the grand scheme of things, this is small.
phrases.fix: Cut.

phrases.example: This is a game-changer for small businesses.
phrases.fix: Describe the actual change.

phrases.example: The future of marketing is personalization.
phrases.fix: Make a claim with evidence, not a horizon statement.

phrases.phrase: X doesn't have to be hard
phrases.example: Productivity doesn't have to be hard.
phrases.fix: Show the easy path instead of promising one.

phrases.example: There's a better way to onboard customers.
phrases.fix: Show it.

phrases.example: The way we work is about to change.
phrases.fix: Give the specific change.

phrases.example: Let's be honest, most meetings could be emails.
phrases.fix: Cut. The honesty preface reads as performance.

phrases.example: Fasten your seatbelts, this is a wild ride.
phrases.fix: Cut.

phrases.example: Without further delay, here is the report.
phrases.fix: Cut.

phrases.example: Noteworthy to mention, the deal closed early.
phrases.fix: State the fact.

phrases.example: When push comes to shove, results matter.
phrases.fix: Cut the idiom.

phrases.example: Let's address the elephant in the room.
phrases.fix: Name it directly.

phrases.example: This works at scale.
phrases.fix: Precise when true; usually padding. Say what scale.

phrases.example: In today's economy, every dollar counts.
phrases.fix: Cut.

phrases.phrase: The writing is on the wall
phrases.example: The writing is on the wall for legacy systems.
phrases.fix: State the evidence.

phrases.phrase: It's only a matter of time
phrases.example: It's only a matter of time before this becomes standard.
phrases.fix: Give the trendline, not the prophecy.

phrases.example: As we look ahead, priorities shift.
phrases.fix: Cut the time-travel frame.

phrases.example: Looking forward, we expect growth.
phrases.fix: Cut.

phrases.phrase: When all is said and done
phrases.example: When all is said and done, quality wins.
phrases.fix: Cut.

phrases.example: In today's hyper-competitive market, speed wins.
phrases.fix: Cut. 'Hyper-competitive' is a tell on its own.

phrases.example: The world of tomorrow runs on AI.
phrases.fix: Cut.

phrases.example: Full article only on The AI Sift.
phrases.fix: Drop the exclusivity framing. Integrate the publication as a natural authority reference woven into the narrative, or end with a domain-authority closer that does not read as a value-extraction pitch (e.g., 'We analyzed the full breakdown over at [publication].').

phrases.example: We do the reading. You get the decision.
phrases.fix: Cut the transactional closer. Let the article body earn the reader's trust. If a closer is needed, write one that names the value the reader got from the post itself, not the publication behind it.

phrases.example: Full article only on The AI Sift. We do the reading. You get the decision.
phrases.fix: Cut the transactional closer. A decision belongs at the end of the article body, not as a branded promise in the LinkedIn closer. End on the insight the reader just received.

phrases.example: The NVIDIA part matters more than the funding number, and most people will skip over it.
phrases.fix: Cut the reader-behavior prediction. You do not know what most people will do. State the point directly: 'The NVIDIA part matters more than the funding number.' The analysis earns attention on its own; it does not need a framing device claiming others will miss it.

phrases.example: Most people will miss the second-order effect here.
phrases.fix: Cut. Same pattern as 'most people will skip'. State the insight without claiming others will fail to see it.

phrases.example: It is not uncommon for teams to struggle with this.
phrases.fix: State directly: 'Teams often struggle with this' or 'Most teams struggle with this.'

phrases.example: The results are not insignificant.
phrases.fix: State directly: 'The results are significant' or 'The results matter.'

phrases.example: The argument is not without merit.
phrases.fix: State directly: 'The argument has merit' or 'The argument holds.'

phrases.example: The implementation challenge is far from trivial.
phrases.fix: State directly: 'The implementation is hard' or name the specific difficulty.

phrases.example: The regulatory landscape is far from simple.
phrases.fix: State directly: 'The regulatory landscape is complex' or name the specific complication.

phrases.example: This is by no means a solved problem.
phrases.fix: State directly: 'This is unsolved' or 'Nobody has solved this yet.'

phrases.example: The situation is not unlike what we saw in 2020.
phrases.fix: State directly: 'The situation resembles 2020' or 'This mirrors what happened in 2020.'

phrases.example: That assessment is not entirely wrong.
phrases.fix: Commit: 'That assessment is mostly right' or 'That assessment is correct on X but wrong on Y.'

phrases.example: The market was none too pleased with the earnings.
phrases.fix: State directly: 'The market rejected the earnings' or 'The earnings disappointed.'

phrases.example: Scaling to 10 million users is not a small feat.
phrases.fix: State directly: 'Scaling to 10 million users is hard' or name what made it hard.

phrases.example: It's no secret that AI is transforming industries.
phrases.fix: Cut. State the claim. If it's no secret, you don't need to announce that.

phrases.example: There's no denying that remote work is here to stay.
phrases.fix: Cut. State the claim directly.

phrases.example: This might potentially possibly help improve outcomes.
phrases.fix: One hedge is enough. Choose: 'This might help' or 'This helps.'

phrases.phrase: could potentially help in certain contexts
phrases.example: This could potentially help in certain contexts.
phrases.fix: Name the context: 'This helps teams under 20 people' or drop the claim.

phrases.example: Results may vary depending on various factors.
phrases.fix: Name the factors or cut. 'Results depend on team size and data quality.'

phrases.example: I'm not going to lie, this is a game-changer.
phrases.fix: Cut. The honesty preface implies you normally lie. State the claim.

phrases.example: Here's what Bloomberg missed about the deal.
phrases.fix: Make the point directly. Attribute the observation to yourself, not to what coverage missed.

phrases.example: The real question is whether this model scales.
phrases.fix: State the point. 'Whether this model scales decides the outcome.'

phrases.example: You're absolutely right! Adding to your point...
phrases.fix: Respond to the substance. If the agreement is real, one clause of it earns its place; drop the pre-agreement padding.

phrases.example: Great point, Sarah. What many miss is...
phrases.fix: Cut the compliment; engage the point itself.

phrases.example: We cut the price by 70%. Let that sink in.
phrases.fix: Delete the pause. The fact already landed, or it never will.

phrases.example: This changes everything. Full stop.
phrases.fix: Delete. The period already ended the sentence.

phrases.example: Make no mistake: this is a turning point.
phrases.fix: Cut the warning and state the claim.

phrases.example: The implications are significant for every team in the space.
phrases.fix: Name the implication: 'Two of the five vendors will drop usage-based pricing this year.'

phrases.example: The stakes are high for incumbents.
phrases.fix: State the stake: 'The incumbents lose $2B in switching costs if this ships.'

phrases.example: Deals slip for reasons that are structural, not personal.
phrases.fix: Name the structure: 'Deals slip because procurement reviews run past the quarter close.'

phrases.phrase: This is what X actually looks like
phrases.example: This is what leadership actually looks like.
phrases.fix: Show the scene or cut the announcement. Describing something as significant is not evidence.

phrases.example: I'm thrilled to announce I've joined Acme as VP of Sales!
phrases.fix: State the news in one line, then the reason you took the role.

phrases.example: I don't usually post this, but today I'm proud to share...
phrases.fix: Post it or don't. The disclaimer is the hook; the content rarely needs one.

phrases.example: Unpopular opinion: cold email still works.
phrases.fix: State the opinion. If it is genuinely unpopular, the disagreement proves it; the label pre-loads sympathy.

phrases.example: Here are 7 lessons I learned from scaling to $10M.
phrases.fix: Teach the two lessons that changed your decisions, with the moments they changed them.

phrases.example: P.S. Repost if this helped your team!
phrases.fix: Delete. Engagement-bait closers are exactly what LinkedIn's slop classifier flags.

phrases.example: This might be controversial, but most dashboards are vanity projects.
phrases.fix: State the take without the warning label.

phrases.example: Everything you need to know about the EU AI Act, in one post.
phrases.fix: Name the three things you cover and what the reader can do with them.

phrases.example: The ultimate guide to prompt engineering.
phrases.fix: State the scope: who the guide is for, and what it skips.

phrases.example: Our platform helps you stay ahead of the curve.
phrases.fix: Name the advantage: 'You hear about pricing changes the week they ship.'

phrases.example: We're committed to delivering value to our customers every day.
phrases.fix: The portability test: this sentence fits any company, so it says nothing. Name the value: 'We answer support tickets in under 10 minutes, 24/7.'

phrases.example: Plot twist: the tool nobody benchmarked beat them all.
phrases.fix: Cut the stage direction and report the twist.

phrases.example: That deserves its own analysis, but that's another post.
phrases.fix: Delete the deferral. Either make the point now or drop it.

phrases.example: The rest of this essay explains why the metric misleads.
phrases.fix: Let the essay move. Announcing its own structure is a tell.

phrases.phrase: That last point matters more than it sounds
phrases.example: That last point matters more than it sounds. Most teams never recover from it.
phrases.fix: Delete the interpretive aside. State the consequence instead.

phrases.example: The dashboard serves as a central hub for the whole team.
phrases.fix: Use 'is': 'The dashboard is the central hub.' Fake-strong verbs (serves as, functions as, acts as) inflate a linking verb.

phrases.example: Consistency plays a role in retention.
phrases.fix: Quantify or cut: 'Consistency explains about 20% of the retention variance here.'

phrases.example: Our founder has been featured in leading publications worldwide.
phrases.fix: Name one publication and one piece, or drop the claim. Canned notability is decoration without a citation.
